utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I gather that as it is hailing outside we are to be besieged with submissions inside. Who's going to go first? Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The Prosecution has just two brief administrative matters to inform the Court, Trial Chamber. Prosecution exhibit P490, when it was admitted it was admitted with a draft English translation and the final English translation has now been produced and updated -- excuse me, uploaded in can e-court and therefore we simply ask that the draft English translation of this exhibit be replaced with a final English translation which has the document identification number N000-7279-ET.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, secondly, Your Honour, with respect to the exhibit that has been marked for identification as P00379, which you may recall, is the series of documents produced by the investigative commission of the Ministry of Interior of Macedonia during 2003. The -- it was -- we realised a day or two day ago that on e-court there was a portion of the range of documents that had not actually been uploaded into e-court. And so it is now my understanding that the full range of these materials has now been uploaded into e-court, and I just wanted to bring that to the Chamber's attention. The Chamber has already dealt with these materials. They've reviewed them in the binders and during testimony of the Prosecution witnesses. It is simply we have now provided a full version in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, indeed. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We will hail further on the Trial Chamber, given the opportunity. We would simply announce that we've received from CLSS what is admitted as exhibit P485. There was quite a significant translation issue at page I believe 18 of the document where there was a reference to "implicit capabilities," which should in fact read as "no demonstrated compatibilities" and I'm announcing that, Your Honour, because the correct translation of the document may be used with Mr. Ostreni in the course of this day or on Monday, if the cross-examination is not finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I would like to briefly announce and inform the court in order to have a better planning of the trial, I would like to inform the Honourable Tribunal that the 7th January is the Orthodox Christmas and since the accused Johan Tarculovski and Mr. Boskoski as well as the Defence counsels of both, they celebrate the 7th of January as a Christmas, so therefore we would like to request from Your Honours if the 7 of January is proclaimed a day off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is not the sort of submission that we had anticipated. We are certainly conscious of the major festivals affecting counsel and accused, and there is also the Orthodox New Year although perhaps not as significant as the one in some other areas of the Christian following. The Chamber is looking with some anxiety at exactly where the trial will be, depending on when the Prosecution case might finish, whether or not there is to be anticipated a submission from either or both accused under 98 bis, the time that will be necessary for both Defences, if the trial is to proceed, to comply with the procedural requirements before the Defence case can commence, and what would be a reasonable time to allow to the Defence for their final preparation before their cases get under way. And all of that is going to be complicated by this vacation here of three weeks, and then, as you mention, the Orthodox celebrations. So there are a number of factors we have to weigh against a background that we don't want to lose time unnecessarily. But we do respect the need and the appropriateness of celebrations of significance such as those that you have mentioned. Now, I think probably it's a little premature today to be thinking about some of those issues, particularly as it is as yet not clear when the Prosecution case will finish, which is the starting point for all those other matters. Go, though, with some warm heart, Mr. Apostolski, that the Chamber would not be minded to sit on the day of the Orthodox Christmas, whatever else happens. Can we leave it at that --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, for taking the time for this, but I believed that maybe it was the best time to inform the Court. Anyway, thank you very much for listening to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have already determined the Macedonian Orthodox celebration date, because we have been looking at all of these issues, but thank you for bringing it up. We will certainly, from the Chamber's point of view, be looking at this with a lot more purpose once it is clear when the Prosecution case can conclude and we can move into these other areas, because we have to allow appropriate time for Defence to prepare, but we don't want to waste time at that break. Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The excitement of the moment, Ms. Regue you thought that you had concluded your evidence. We left the door a little ajar in case, overnight, you thought of something.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours I leave that -- we leave it as it was. So we have no further questions. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, are you ready to proceed, if we can find a witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are now ready to proceed, and it is Mr. Mettraux who will now be asking you some questions. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon Mr. Ostreni. My name is Guenael Mettraux, and together with my colleague Edina Residovic I'm appearing on behalf of Mr. Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot hear the interpretation well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I will talk for a little while and you tell me when you can hear an interpretation, Mr. Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I can hear it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Splendid. And could I remind you that the affirmation you made still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ostreni. My name is Guenael Mettraux and together with my colleague Edina Residovic I'm appearing on behalf of Mr. Boskoski. Mr. Ostreni, you have indicated to the Prosecution that you were appointed to be the Chief of Staff of the National Liberation Army sometimes towards the end of March 2001. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that I probably said March 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at the time you indicated that you were given the rank of general of the NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the transformation of the KLA, then with the KPC and with the same rank, I joined the UCK of Macedonia, the National Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply to clarify, as you joined the NLA, you were given the rank of general of that organisation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The post was that of a general.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the person who appointed you to that position was Mr. Ali Ahmeti. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you tell the Chamber based on what law did Mr. Ahmeti appoint you to that position?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Based on the idea of transforming the uprising into an army, an army that would require a General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Mr. Ostreni. Could you indicate what law, if any, Mr. Ahmeti had relied upon to give you the title and the rank of a general in the National Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there was no law on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know who had appointed Mr. Ahmeti to be the so-called Supreme Commander of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came from the United States of America on the 26th of February, I met with Mr. Ali Ahmeti in March. He was with some friends of his. And he said that the uprising has already begun and that they had begun to organise themselves and they invited me to join.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, Mr. Ostreni. But do you know who had appointed Mr. Ahmeti to be the so-called Supreme Commander of the NLA; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The friends, the comrades he worked with, he cooperated with, and his commitment and engagement made all the others accept him as their leader, including myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that as was the case with your appointment, his selection, to call it that, as the Supreme Commander was not based on any particular law or regulation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that there was no law on this issue, because, as I said, this was an uprising, an ongoing uprising and it was seeking a form of organisation so that it would continue operating in an organised and planned manner in order to fulfil its goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that Mr. Ahmeti, unlike yourself, is not a military trained man, is that correct, he is not a military man by training?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge on whether he is trained or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that prior to your selection to be the Chief of Staff of the Main Staff of the NLA, no one had held that position; in other words, you were the first person to be given that position. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not told that there was someone there at that post before me, so I must be the first one at that function. I have no knowledge of any other before me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you receive any written order or any written decision appointing you to that position from Mr. Ahmeti?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not receive it in writing. I received it orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So in effect there would be no paper trail or paper indication of the time and the basis on which you had been appointed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a document, but all the documents that I prepared were adopted by Mr. Ali Ahmeti and in my opinion, this is a fact that proves that I was general -- correction, head of General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Do you recall, Mr. Ostreni, to indicate to the Prosecution that prior to your being chosen to be the Chief of Staff of the NLA, the NLA consisted of a number of small groups operating without cooperation and that you tried to bring some degree of organisation. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is true. This was at least my impression. As I already mentioned, I returned on 26th or 27th of February to Skopje from the United States. In March I met Mr. Ali Ahmeti, and at that time my impression was that the NLA was composed of groups that were operative but that required notification of reorganisation and taking a certain direction and be controlled.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that although you were given the title of a general and the position of a Chief of Staff, you in fact were given no power in that organisation and were left completely out of the loop about what was going on in your organisation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree perhaps that your appointment as a Chief of Staff of the NLA was a public exercise, a public relation exercise by Mr. Ahmeti to put a more respectable face on the NLA and in particular, that of a military man. Do you agree that is what happened?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree that is what happened. I believe that Mr. Ali Ahmeti needed a person who was expert in this field and who would contribute to the organisation to become what it should become and be under control.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to go back to a number of statements which you've made yesterday and in your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor about the efforts that you say you made to ensure an enforced discipline and standard of humanitarian law in your organisation, and I'm going to put a number of propositions to you and you are going to tell me whether you agree with those or not. I understand your evidence to be, Mr. Ostreni, that there was a functioning chain of command from Mr. Ahmeti and yourself down to the member of your organisation in the field. Is that correct? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that also your evidence that your organisation was applying and respecting the Geneva Conventions and other humanitarian law standards and that you even issued a so-called communique to that effect. Is that correct? Is it that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my evidence that we were always committed to -- for things to become the way you described -- you described them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that also your evidence, Mr. Ostreni, that you enforced within your organisation strict standards of military discipline, and I think you've indicated that those who would breach those standards would be held responsible. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I understood your evidence properly, your attachment to these various matters was important for you to show that your organisation was in fact an army and not a criminal or terrorist gang, as it sometimes is referred to. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that our entire work and efforts were directed at achieving the goal of creating an army, the National Liberation Army, which would be controlled, organised, disciplined and which would carry out the tasks and duties received from the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ostreni. And did you or Mr. Ahmeti gave any orders or order to comply with those standards of humanitarian law which you said you were attached to?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is regulated by the rules and the rule -- the rules of service, that is, and the order issued by Mr. Ali Ahmeti for the implementation of the rules of service is simultaneously an order for-- to comply with what you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this order would include, for instance, a prohibition on murdering people. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All our units were prohibited to abuse office or kill civilians. Their duties were limited to carrying out on their military duties respectively in combat with the ARM and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And you would agree that this regulations and the order that accompanied it would also prohibit the members of your organisation from kidnapping people or committing ethnic cleansing. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our rules did not allow for this in any way and we didn't have or maintain such a position. On the contrary, our position was to safeguard the life of the civilians and their property.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And I suppose the regulations and the order accompanying it would also prohibit the destruction of religion buildings or their use as military facilities as well as the sexual abuse of civilians. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Abuse and destruction were prohibited especially desecration of religious building. However, facilities and buildings used by the ARM and the police were our objectives.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that. But as far as the NLA is concerned, you would agree that you made it quite clear to the members of your organisation that using religion facilities, for example, as military facilities would be an illegal act and a crime. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, because our rules of service clearly stated that our soldiers and units could use social facilities, such as schools, for example, and civilian buildings, but upon approval received from the owners of those buildings or facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you or Mr. Ahmeti issue any order or regulation to the effect that disciplinary steps or other measures would be taken against members of your organisation that would breach those standards?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not Mr. Ahmeti, honourable counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Mr. Ostreni. I'd realised that, and perhaps is a word that has been miss in the translation. I was asking whether yourself, Mr. Ostreni, or your colleague Mr. Ahmeti at any stage issued any order or regulation to the effect that disciplinary steps or any other measures would be taken against members of your organisation that would breach those standards.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rules envisaged disciplinary measures to be taken by the battalion or brigade commander in case members of their respective units breach the rules of service of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And I think you have explained yesterday that the importance of those standards and the various regulations which you say were adopted at the time was to ensure that the hierarchy of your organisation functioned properly and that the good order of the organisation was maintained. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That is a rule of each and every rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You would agree, I hope, Mr. Ostreni, that an organisation that would use crime and terrorism as a way to achieve its purposes or its goals could not be regarded as an army as you understand it. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are thinking that the NLA is a terrorist organisation that has committed crimes, I do not agree with that proposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. But would you agree with the more general proposition, Mr. Ostreni, that an organisation, whatever its name or label, that would use crime and terrorism as a way to achieve its goals and purposes could not be regarded as an army, as you, a military man, understand it. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The source for the establishment of the NLA is the uprising which should be regulated, governed, have its hierarchy and description of responsibilities and duty to prevent it from committing any terrorist acts or crimes, because in that event, it would have been very detrimental to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ostreni. If you could try to answer the more general question that I'm asking you. Setting aside for a moment the specific situation of the NLA, we're going to come back to the NLA in a moment, but putting it aside, would you agree with the proposition that an organisation that would use crime and terrorism to achieve its goal and purposes could not possibly be regarded as an army, as you, a military man, understands it. Do you agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it uses or resorts to terrorism, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what about an organisation that would have recourse to crime, Mr. Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not very clear about what you put to me. That has resource to crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I apologise for not being any clearer, Mr. Ostreni. I'll give you an example, perhaps. Would you agree that an organisation that would use, for instance, murders, kidnapping, or ethnic cleansing to achieve its goal and purposes could not be regarded as an army, as you understand it. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it does what are you saying, yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And you've indicated to my colleague of the Prosecution that you kept in touch with the so-called commanders of your so-called brigades through daily telephone contacts. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And during those telephone contacts, I believe you said that the brigade commanders, as they are known, would inform you -- would inform you about what was going on in their areas of responsibility. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct also, Mr. Ostreni, that rather than trying to install within the National Liberation Army a military-like sort of discipline among its members, Mr. Ahmeti and the other leaders of that organisation in fact used crime, violence against civilians, and terrorist attacks as a way to achieve its purposes. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not informed of this, and I don't agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in fact is it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that you have told the Office of the Prosecutor that you had no knowledge of any crime or breach of discipline that occurred within your organisation, the NLA, during the crisis period in 2001. Do you recall telling that to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I said that. That was a general statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But surely, Mr. Ostreni, as a so-called Chief of Staff of the NLA, you would know that a relatively large number of civilians had been kidnapped by members of your organisation. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that. And I'm saying that they were not kidnapped by the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D733, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, I'm going to show you a document that comes from the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia and there will be a Macedonian version of the document on your right. I apologise, we don't have an Albanian translation of that document. I will read it out to you. That may assist you. This is a document dated the 29th of August of 2001 and it comes from the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Macedonia, the headquarters of operative action Ramno and it is being sent to the crisis management centre in Skopje and the subject is submission of requested data. Are you able to follow, Mr. Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I am. It's a little bit difficult for me, because it is only in Macedonian, but can I follow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will read the passages to you, Mr. Ostreni, that may assist you and if you need a paper copy, can you certainly ask me. I have a paper copy for you. The text goes on to say this: "With a telegram from 29 August 2001 you have urgently requested data to be submitted to you about the kidnapped persons who are still being held captive by the Albanian terrorist groups. In the files kept at the Ministry of Internal Affairs, based on information acquired from the file, we hereby submit to you the following." And then there follows an overview of persons who are considered to have been kidnapped by the Albanian terrorist groups. And there's a list of name of those people. Mr. Ostreni, were you aware during the crisis in 2001 that your organisation, the NLA, was kidnapping civilians or members of the Macedonian security forces? Is that something you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of the fact that there were people who were imprisoned, members of Brigade 113 and 115, who, after the war, were released from jail in the presence of international community. I don't know which organisation it was, maybe the Red Cross, or some other. I know that 13 were being asked for and that 15 persons were released.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, Mr. Ostreni. But I was asking whether you knew about civilians and members of the Macedonian security forces who had been kidnapped by members of your organisation, the so-called NLA. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed, but they were not kidnapped; they were captured as war prisoners. The others had entered the territory controlled by the brigade to collect information. They were detained in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, thank you. When you say that they were not kidnapped but captured as prisoners of war, are you aware of the fact, Mr. Ostreni, that many of those people who had been kidnapped by your organisation were never found? Is that something which is within your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any information. I know only about those persons, that the NLA, after signing the Ohrid Agreement has released. As I said, either the Red Cross or some other organisation came there to take over such persons so they went back to their families. Among them there were paramilitaries. Ramero [phoen] was one, another soldier who surrendered himself to the NLA. He didn't want to go back to his own forces. I know that the spokesperson talked with him directly. He said he is enjoying a good health and he declared this publicly on television and for the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So no one within your organisation provided you with information that a number of those kidnapped persons had been executed and buried by members of your organisation for example in and around the town of Neprosteno. That's not information that was given to you?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neprosteno is not a town, it's a village, and I was not informed neither then or now that someone had kidnapped civilian citizens I don't have any information to that effect, nor that they were executed, as you put it. We heard something about this event after the war but they were -- the NLA soldiers or their superiors were not involved in anything. At least I don't have any information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that, Mr. Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D16, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And one thing -- another thing, if I may. In the table that I saw on the screen, it doesn't write that it is accurate. It is written only that it is believed that they were kidnapped. Can you show it again, please, the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the document be shown to Mr. Ostreni again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll read to you perhaps the passage you're referring upon. It's just under the title, Mr. Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second. I will read it in Macedonian. It is written here, Preglat, which means table, then the names of person who are believed to have been kidnapped by terrorist, Albanian terrorist groups, so this document doesn't say that it is a fact, that it is certain, but it is believed, it says. Everyone has a right to believe or to think what he or she thinks or wants. But before stating something we must be certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps the next document will help you, Mr. Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's Exhibit 1D16.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is a document that is in the English language again and I will read it out to you. It's a -- the record of an e-mail, if you wish, that comes from the organisation known as the OSCE and it's been provided to us by the Office of the Prosecutor. And the person who is writing this e-mail on the 10th of July of 2001, is an employee of the OSCE. Says that she's working on a supplemental report that will address recent developments. She says the allegations with regard to the alleged human rights violation by the ethnic Albanian armed group have increased and now include, and I will read out to you the first two on this list. It says that it includes the illegal detention of civilians, and she mentioned notably Tetovo, Radusa, and the Matejce area. Before going any further, Mr. Ostreni, are you aware or were you given any information by your so-called chain of command about cases of illegal detention of civilians in any of those three areas, Tetovo, Radusa, or Matejce?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said to you that we had information that in Radush and in Brigade 113 there were people who were detained, who were released after the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement. Six years have passed since that time, I remember this, but I don't know anything about Tetovo. Maybe there was also someone there who was detained. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And were you aware that those detained persons were civilians, Mr. Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information that we received from the brigades said that these persons were tasked with collection of information on the situation of the brigades, their positions, supplies, movements and so on. So it was believed that these persons were working for the intelligence service. You yourself said that some of these persons were employed by various security bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, did you try to find out, Mr. Ostreni, as Chief of Staff of the NLA what the status of those persons were? Did you make any effort in that sense?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to find out, and my instructions and those of my commander were to treat people fairly, to take care of their health and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that. I'll bring you to the second point on this e-mail which is still in front of you. It also records cases of forced labour, detained person report, they are forced to dig ditches, ethnic Albanians sometimes report they are similarly forced to assist NLA actions. Do you know of any such case, Mr. Ostreni, which would have been reported back to you by your colleagues about cases of forced labour within your organisation, the NLA? Is that information that you received?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't receive any such information of people being forced to dig trenches or something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You would agree that any such conduct if it had taken place would be contrary to Geneva Conventions and other humanitarian standards. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not necessary to force them to work, unless they helped to -- to put up their -- the place where they were staying, because people had to be sheltered somewhere. If you mean something else, I don't think it is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, just a general proposition, Mr. Ostreni, would you agree that forcing people to assist the NLA or, in particular, by forcing them to dig ditches for the NLA would be contrary to the standards recognised by the Geneva Conventions. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that. But I believe they were not forced to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall yesterday, Mr. Ostreni, you told my colleague from the Prosecution that in your view the NLA had a fighting edge, to call it that, because contrary to the Macedonian forces, your organisation was made up of volunteers. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But in fact the reason why you said that, Mr. Ostreni, is to hide something much more embarrassing which was going on in your organisation at the time, which was the forced conscription of young Albanian citizens. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single Albanian was forced to participate in the NLA. On the contrary, everyone had the right, whenever he so wished, to hand in the weapon and go home or wherever he wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, that's part of the NLA propaganda, isn't it, of a large popular support within the Albanian population, but the reality, Mr. Ostreni, is that you used violence and threats on to your own ethnic group, the Albanian ethnic group to have fighters in your organisation and where people refused to cooperate you used crime and violence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is an insult to us. This is an observation that you are making to throw mud at Albanians and at the NLA. Even today, the NLA and what it did is honoured by the Albanians. If we had acted the way you are putting it, we wouldn't be able to face our own citizens, so I do not at all agree with your proposition and I want to say again that this is an insult against the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Ostreni, I'll bring your attention to point 3 of the e-mail which is in front of you, and it comes, not from the Defence but from the OSCE, and it records the following incidents involving the NLA. It says: "Forced conscription, there are report one person was killed and several wounded when a father resisted the attempt to forcibly conscript his son into the NLA." Mr. Ostreni, are you aware of this case or any similar case within the NLA where violence was used to force people to join your organisation?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such cases, namely, of using force against people who wanted -- who didn't want to join the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's go back to the kidnapped people for a second, Mr. Ostreni. Are you aware that the European Union set up a specific commission whose role and function it was to sort out the issue of the disappeared and kidnapped during the crisis. Do you know about this commission?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Maybe you're aware perhaps that your colleague, Mr. Ahmeti, and a number of other so-called commanders of the NLA met with members of that commission. Is it something you know?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I don't have any information. Excuse me, Mr. Ahmeti, at the end of the war, talked about the release of all detainees kept by the brigades. I want to repeat it. Together we went to Brigade 113 and 115 and those persons were being detained were released and went their own ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of Mr. Ahmeti attending meetings of this European commission in the early month of the year 2002 and pretending to be interested in solving the issues of those people who had not yet reappeared. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about that in 2002. I know that they were working to try to find a solution to this problem, find the problems [as interpreted] who were missing. One of them is also the uncle of Mr. Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ostreni. But at this stage I will stay with the people who had disappeared and who were suspected to have been kidnapped by the NLA. Were you aware that in March 2002 there was still quite a large number of people who had not reappeared? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In March of 2001?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Of 2002, Mr. Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In March of 2002, I was following attempts being made to find the person -- the missing persons. Even to this day Mr. Ali Ahmeti is willing - me, too - are willing to help if we learn something in relation to this issue, because among the missings are not only Macedonian civilians but also Albanians and all of them are citizens of the Republic of Macedonia. So everyone must contribute to finding them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that that sort of statement that you just made, Mr. Ostreni, is just for the public. You don't mean a word you've just said. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to say what I already said. When I talk, I don't think in two ways. I express what comes to my mind, what I think. I speak the way I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D745, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is a document which we've received from the Office of the Prosecutor, and it's the record of a meeting which this European commission on kidnapped and other meeting -- missing persons had in -- on the 25th [sic] of March of 2002 and there's a number of passages of that meeting that I would like to read to you. First it explains that the purpose of the meeting is that "the commission continues its effort to find out the fate of the 20 missing persons." And it says: "In connection with both the MOI and the former NLA, we are now trying to clarify a number of question that both parties have been unable to answer so far." Then in the next paragraph it refers to a meeting that took place the 15, apparently, of that month and it says this: "On 15th we met with Ahmeti and he promised us his support in making the different commanders available for us to meet them. And it says: "When talking to Luli last week he explained that his authority in the structure is weak and he said that it would be easier for the commission to obtain information that for him." And then the member of the commission that prepared that report records himself as saying: "I would like to appeal to you and the former NLA to come forward with information that could solving these cases. I would like to remind you that our task is not a criminal investigation, but we have a humanitarian task. We are therefore not interested in who is guilty of what, but only in receiving information that can help us to clarify the fate of these 20 missing persons. This information can be forwarded also anonymously." And then if you go further down the page, in fact, we ask the assistance of the registry, there's a passage, Mr. Ostreni, you may be able to locate it which starts with the words: "Cela further told the commission." Can you see that? I will read it out to you. It says this: "Cela further told the commission that the former NLA has serious problems with obtaining information about missing persons. None of their former commanders seem to possess the information or are reluctant to tell the truth." And just stopping for a comment, is it correct that Cela was one of the so-called brigade commander of the NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know Cela to be a member of the NLA, Mr. Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you indicate what position he held during the crisis?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked in the G2 and, at the same time he was in 112th Brigade but he was not, as you're putting it, a brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for the clarification. And could you perhaps indicate what the name of that person is, Mr. Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cela?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Hazbi Lika.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And the document goes on to say this: "Cela promised however to send the message through the former NLA that the leadership thinks it is important to solve this issue but suggested at the same time that further conversations with commanders be conducted by the commission." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that this suggests that the NLA was in fact quite keen to assist the commission. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm reading the interpretation of what you're reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, Mr. Ostreni, do you agree that the passage or the statement attributed to Cela that I have just read out to you suggests a willingness on the part of the NLA to assist the commission in finding out what happened to the kidnapped and missing persons. Do you agree that's what the statement of Cela suggests?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with what you're saying, that the NLA, or people who were members of the NLA, were willing to find the missing persons. And, as I understand, Cela is saying that there will be contribution for the -- finding solution to the issue of the missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if we can turn to the next page you will see the assessment of the member of the commission who prepared that report. I will read it out to you, Mr. Ostreni. The comment by the person is this: "It seems that no one in the former NLA is interested in solving this issue. In the last meeting with Ahmeti, he referred all detailed questions to Luli and only said that he is interested in solving this issue. In the last meeting with Luli he complained that he does not have the authority needed to obtain the information or to send messages through the organisation. Luli suggested us at that time to talk with Cela." Isn't that correct that the reality of what was and has been happening, Mr. Ostreni, is that your organisation publicly pretends to be assisting in issues such as this one but in fact does nothing about it. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that, because of the following. As I said earlier, it is not only ethnic Macedonians missing but ethnic Albanians as well, citizens of the Republic of Macedonia. And the NLA making no difference or distinction between the two, including Mr. Ali Ahmeti, they were trying to find information to the extent it was possible and inform the commission and talk to its members on this issue. This interest continues to be shown in this respect because still there is no information about the missing persons and as I said earlier, one of them is the uncle of Mr. Ali Ahmeti. I think his name is Rushdi.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that the commission of crimes and acts of terrorism by your organisation, the so-called NLA, was not just an unfortunate consequence of the war or an armed conflict but it was in fact the strategy of your organisation to commit such crime to attain such goals. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there's no way I can agree with this. This is absolutely contrary to the goals of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But setting aside the stated goals of your organisation, Mr. Ostreni, do you agree that what happened on the ground is perfectly consistent with an organisation that is using crimes to terrorise civilians and cleanse areas from other ethnic groups. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot agree with this and this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall yesterday being asked questions by my colleague about what you called was the "control exercised by your organisation in number of locations in which the NLA was active." Do you recall those questions?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I believe I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that you explained to the Chamber and to the Prosecution prior to that, that your organisation or members of your organisation were exercising some sort of authority within those areas. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have pointed out the zones, and these zones are documented. The Chamber has them and I believe you have them as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. And you agree that what those areas have in common, Mr. Ostreni, is that in all of them your organisation used the same practice. You cleansed those areas from other ethnic groups, members of other ethnic groups so that you were able to impose your authority over a very docile population. Do you agree that's what happened?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot agree with this and I will not agree with this. Because facts point out of a different situation. What the academy of science did, which was supported by certain politicians regarding partition of the Republic of Macedonia and the change of population actually infiltrated fear among the population. This is first. Secondly, the internal organs, that is to say, the police, began to distribute weapons to the Macedonian civilians in order to defend themselves and this also caused fear amongst the population. That's why a number of civilians went to see the president, the late president, Mr. Trajkovski, in the company of a member of the parliament known as Bomba. From their statements it is clear where this insecurity of the civilians comes from. In our view, this insecurity was caused by the way the state organs, the police and army were operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that, Mr. Ostreni. Is it correct that your group, the NLA, in June 2001 entered the town or city of Aracinovo? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was information provided back to you by your colleagues who were in Aracinovo about what was going on in the town or city at that time?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The NLA forces had entered part of Haracin, and they were getting ready to defend themselves, expecting an attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So surely you would have received reports from those people you talked to, that as soon as your colleagues entered the town they started scaring away the local population. Did you receive any such reports?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, could the witness please be shown what is Exhibit 1D259, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is a document that is dated the 14th of June of 2001. And it's a summary that was given to the Defence by a particular embassy about the events in Aracinovo and I will read to what you the summary of that document says. It says this: "The Macedonian government virtually abdicates control of the town of Aracinovo to the insurgents. The occupation of the village highlights the ineptness and impotence of the security forces." Can you locate that, Mr. Ostreni? This is at the beginning of the page.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is in English. I don't know English very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I apologise for that, Mr. Ostreni. In that case I will read the passage to you verbatim.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. It's not enough to apologise. I want to be familiarised with the document you're asking me about and I want to know what I'm talking about here. Because there might be a word there saying it is believed or it is thought, and you might put that word to me as it is something like a fact. So I want to know what I'm talking about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Ostreni, I will speak under the control of my colleagues of the Prosecution and the Judges of this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry to turn to the next page, please. And if we could go -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will read a sentence to you, Mr. Ostreni, and then I will ask you a question about this. It says this: "According to local inhabitants, sometime during the afternoon of Friday, 8 June 2001, approximately 30 members of the NLA (supposedly not from the town itself, per comments from all residents of the town) entered the town and began scaring the inhabitants out of the town, especially the ethnic Macedonian inhabitants ..." My question to you is this, Mr. Ostreni: Did you receive any reports from the members of your organisation where in Aracinovo that some members of this organisation were involved in scaring inhabitants out of the town, especially the ethnic Macedonian inhabitants. Did you receive any such information?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the information that I received was that the unit entered Haracin and not that it was scaring the population away. It was war. If the population was scared of this war, that is a different issue. But if this is a passage from a longer text then it would be difficult for me to answer you. I cannot speak of a single room when I'm not familiar with the building. That's why I need to have this document in the Albanian to be able to read it and understand it, and then you can ask me about that document. You are reading parts of the document to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you perhaps a more general question, which may be easier for you to answer, Mr. Ostreni. Would you agree that should members of a particular group intentionally scare civilians away, that would constitute a violations of humanitarian law. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this is a fragment. The operation should be reviewed in a full context. Part of the NLA brigade forces were in Haracin, which was not defended by the ARM forces. They established their control there and, to me, they performed a task that was given to them by the brigade. And now you're asking me if they scared the civilians away, and you are putting the emphasis on the Macedonian citizens. If you are separating only the Macedonian citizens, this is a tendentious issue. You are putting me in a situation and trying to make me play with words.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's set aside for a moment, Mr. Ostreni, the issue of Aracinovo and let me ask you more general question which doesn't apply to this particular scenario perhaps. Would you agree that the intentional scaring away of civilians, in particular civilians of one ethnic group by armed individuals would be inconsistent with humanitarian law. Do you agree with this general proposition?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree, but I don't have any knowledge that NLA units undertook activities with the aim of scaring away only the known Albanian population. This is something that I cannot agree with and cannot accept.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But are you aware, Mr. Ostreni, as a former Chief of Staff of the so-called NLA that this practice of ethnic cleansing of intimidating and scaring civilians away from the areas that -- in which you were active was actually taking place in almost all places where you were active. Were you aware of that, or didn't you have that information at the time?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information was not ethnic cleansing defined as such. You know that 113rd Brigade received several ultimatums of the Ministry of Interior and the Ministry of Defence so that the civilian population could move out from their villages. If you treat this as ethnic cleansing, then that's a different issue. But we did not drive them away. They were at their free will to choose whether they will stay there or whether they will leave their respective homes and the aim of the NLA was never to carry out ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know where the village of Brezno is, Mr. Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The way you are pronouncing it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I think you will have to help me with the pronunciation, Mr. Ostreni. Do you know of a village called Brezno, which is about 60 kilometre west of Skopje towards Tetovo? Do you know any such village?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me help you then.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D1026 [Realtime transcript read in error"1D0216"], please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, what will appear on your screen is something called an investigator's notes. It's, if you wish, a record of an interview which was carried out by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 7th of July of 2001 with two Macedonians, ethnic Macedonians, and it was conducted by an investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor, Mr. Raatikainen. And the person who was interviewed said the follow: "I and my wife have a summer house at Brezno village. Brezno is located about 60 kilometres from Skopje towards Tetovo near Tearce. There are about 80 houses in the village, none of them belonging to the Macedonian Albanians." Do you know of this village, Mr. Ostreni, does that assist you?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know the village. You helped me by reading this and I would be grateful to help you, but I really don't -- I'm not familiar with this village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is it correct, Mr. Ostreni, as you have indicated in your evidence and also in various documents on which you have drawn, that your organisation, the NLA was active around the area near Tetovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to look at the map where I marked the positions. I cannot give you an answer just by heart. I really don't know where this village is situated.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But perhaps you will know where the village of Tearce is. Tearce.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the name of the village?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Tearce, Mr. Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tearce, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that it is located in the vicinity of the town of Tetovo? Do you agree with that? Not far from it.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's nothing to agree about on this. The village is where it is. And if it's close to Tetovo, then it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that's an area where your organisation is active, or was active in 2001. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I will have to look at the map. Probably it was in the area of Tetovo, in the mountainous regions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we'll look at the moment in a moment, Mr. Ostreni. But at that stage we have the document in front of us. I'll just read out to you what the interview we have said to the Prosecution. They said that on the 20th of July I heard from my neighbours in Brezno, Andjelko Apostolski and Jovan Saveski that three UCK members dressed in UCK camouflage uniforms had come to the village to inform the people that they had to leave and that if they wouldn't, some other soldiers would come and force them to leave. The three men had spoken in clear Macedonian language. People left the village around that time." And then the interviewee continues: "However, I decided to go back to the village with my wife and a few neighbours on 1st July to see that our houses were all right. Shortly after we had arrived to the village at around 12.30, at least seven or eight soldiers came to the village dressed in new camouflage uniforms." Then in the next paragraph the following is said: "Some of the soldiers entered the village from the direction where Vojislav Milovski had his house, this is about 100 metres from our house. The UCK soldiers beat Vojislav and took him towards his house. In front of our house they order all of us, myself, my wife, Vojislav Milovski and Zivko Nestorovski on our knees. They started to ask questions about weapons, et cetera. I told them that I had a hunting rifle in the house and they went and took it." He goes on to say: "We were kept on the street on our knees and all the time they were aiming at our heads with their Kalashnikovs. During this time a villager called Boris Magdinovski, who is about 56 years old and half deaf, and who happened to walk on a road about 25 below us." Then it goes on to say: "Two of the soldiers shot at him and Boris fell down. One of the soldiers then went to make sure he was dead. Boris did not carry anything with him when he was shot." "After this they forced us to leave the village in Zivko's car, that is a white Yugo. Again, they told us that we could not return to the village again. We wanted to take our things (money, documents) from the house but were not allowed to do so. I also tried to take our donkey with us but we were told we couldn't because the soldiers owned it now." Mr. Ostreni, did anyone in your so-called chain of command within the NLA provided with you information about the activities of members of your organisation in the village of Brezno? Do you ever receive any such information?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you agree that if this incident really happened, this would again be quite contrary to international humanitarian law and quite contrary to the orders which you say Mr. Ahmeti issued to respect those standards. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that, and if it is the way you are putting it, those persons should be held responsible. But personally I didn't have any information on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. And we will take the first break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Simply for the transcript at page 33 line 13 I was recorded as referring to a document Rule 65 ter 0216. I must have misspoken. This is 1026, Rule 65 ter 1D1026. And I'd ask the registry to please bring up Rule 65 ter 388, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, I promised before break to come back to a map and I will present one to that may help you locate the village of Tearce. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry to focus on the centre of this document, towards the place called Tetovo, please. And if it could be enlarged a little bit more for Mr. Ostreni. Thank you; that's perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, can you locate the town or city of Tetovo on this map?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you go north from Tetovo, can you locate the village the Tearce?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Tearce.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this map, as you can see contains a number of markings and those markings were made by your colleague Mr. Ahmeti when he was interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor, and he highlighted the village of Tearce as a place where the NLA was active at the time. Is it within your knowledge that this village was in fact -- that the NLA, I apologise, was in fact active in that village during the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving on from Tearce, is it correct also that another place, Mr. Ostreni, which you have claimed was under the control of the NLA is the area north of Tetovo and which you had coloured in yellow in your map. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall it. Six years have passed by and I don't have my map in front of me and I find it difficult to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can assist you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown exhibit P487.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, That will be the map that you've been shown yesterday by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be exhibit P487. Thank you. And if the registry could please focus on the left or western side of the map, please, towards the top. Thank you. That should do. Perfect. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, do you recognise the map which you were presented by the Prosecution yesterday?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Although the map is a bit too large, I think, for the screen, are you able to identify the city or the town of Tetovo on that map. Can you locate it?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that above -- well, in fact to the north, to the west and to some extent to the north-east of Tetovo you have coloured in yellow areas which you say were under the control of the NLA as of 13 of June of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to prove full accuracy, I would kindly ask to you use the maps we gave over to NATO. Because in those maps, you can clearly identify the areas that were under the control of the NLA. Here I see many colours, the places are not marked, the type is very small, so I can't find my bearings here. If Your Honours allow me, I would kindly ask to you show me those maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps can I help, Mr. Ostreni. I will ask you a just a general question at this stage. Is it correct that the NLA claimed to be in control of a number of villages and areas in the northern part and the western part of Tetovo? Do you agree with that? And I'm not asking about any particular location, but a more general question. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will answer also in general terms. All the villages in the north and those that were located within the lines that I marked as the front positions of Brigade 112, 13, 14 and the others, all villages were under the control of respective brigades with the exception of some places having forces of the army and the police of the Republic of Macedonia. I think in this map you can see part of the positions of the army and the police. For example, in Kodra e Dialet [phoen] where Brigade 112 was positioned or there is another concentration above Alasec where Brigade 113 was located. But if you ask me a general question, then the general answer would be found in the maps that I submitted on the 5th of July to NATO. Because I -- in this map, I prepared kind of general plan, whereas the one we submitted to NATO was more accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that, Mr. Ostreni. But would you agree that what you call and what your organisation called control of those areas north and west of Tetovo was in fact kept under "your control,", through the ethnic cleansing of ethnic minorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't operate in Kosova, Your Honour, neither in the north nor on the west. You are asking me questions related to Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Ostreni, we must have had a translation issue. I was asking you about the area north and west of Tetovo and I may specify in particular during the month of July of 2001, and the proposition I'm putting to you is that what your control, as you call it, amounted to was the forceful expulsion of other ethnic groups from the area in which you were active. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree with that. I have reports and documents showing that we have given help and assistance to Macedonian citizens in our hospitals, where we have treated also our soldiers, we have provided medical support to them and we have respected these people. So I cannot agree with you. During that time, in that territory, the state, the government left the population without any medical assistance by withdrawing all of its outpatient clinics, so we had over 500 people in the area covered by Brigade 112 who were supposed to take care and provide medical assistance in general. In that context we treated also Macedonian citizens, elderly people for whom we have documents issued by a Dr. Zul Xhelali who operated in that area and it is not true that anyone forced them to leave the area or cleanse the territory. The NLA dealt only with the Armed Forces and the government, that is, the state, of the Republic of Macedonia but not with the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D18, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, the documents that I'm about to show you is a special report prepared by the organisation known as the OSCE, and its title is, Special report: Human rights-related complaints related to the ethnic armed Albanian group in the Tetovo area, and this report is from the month of July of 2001. And I will read a number of passages of this report to you. It says this: "On Friday, July the 20th, the mission human rights specialist spent the day in the Tetovo area continuing to address human rights concerns specifically related to the conduct of the ethnic Albanian armed group in that region. The allegations under investigation related not only to the group's treatment of ethnic Macedonians in the Tetovo area but also towards persons in the ethnic Albanian community who objected to the ethnic armed Albanian group's activities." Then there are three words that I can't read. Mr. Ostreni, I apologise, Mr. Ostreni, I was receiving other information in my earphones. Mr. Ostreni, were you aware or did you receive any report from the members of your organisation who were in Tetovo at the time that such activities were going on in and around Tetovo? Did you receive any such information?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What kind of information are you saying? I'm not clear, what kind of information are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, did you receive any information from members of your organisation who were present in or around the Tetovo area in July of 2001, that members of the so-called NLA were putting pressure on the civilian population and intimidating members of that population to leave the area. Did you receive any such reports?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me read on from this document. It says this: "The mission specialist confirmed reports from the OSCE's Tetovo area monitors that, even during the cease-fire, the ethnic Macedonian civilian population north of Tetovo is under heavy pressure from the ethnic Albanian armed group to leave. This pressure takes the form of kidnappings, temporary detentions and serious persistent forms of intimidation and restrictions on the movement of civilians attempting to engage in ordinary activities such as agriculture, shopping, and going to work." And the report goes on to say: "The conduct of the ethnic Albanian armed group is consistent with an attempt to ethnically cleanse that area." So I'm asking you again the same question, Mr. Ostreni. Did you receive any information from the people who you say were further down the chain of command in your organisation about what they were doing and what sort of activities they were carrying on in or around the area of Tetovo in July of 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't receive any such information to the fact that our units were carrying out such acts. If I did, and what you are saying is true, we should have taken the necessary measures. But, as I said, I didn't have any such information. I'm not saying that I don't trust such reports if they come from such reliable organisation. But I still have to say that I am not able to read it myself either in Albanian or in Macedonian and have a complete idea of the document. You are putting to me only some fragments and I cannot say whether I agreed with it or not, since I don't have an entire view of it in order for me to understand the purpose of preparing such a document. In this case, I would kindly ask Your Honours to take note of the fact that I cannot read all of it and I'm not in a proper position to say yes or no to the questions asked of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Ostreni, I will read them as carefully as can I and if I make a mistake in doing so, I hope to be corrected by my colleagues or the Judges. Is it the case, Mr. Ostreni, that you received --

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, please, I think I am the position of the witness here, and I think it is up to me to say whether I am in a position or not to say yes or no. It -- I should know what it is all about in its entirety to be able to know what the purpose of that document is, not only in this case but also in other cases that you are putting documents to me. I know Albanian and Macedonian, I know a little of English but not more than asking a few simple questions. And you know to -- you want me to say whether I understand it or not, whether I agree with you or not, but I am at a disadvantageous position to comment on such crucial matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if a question raise any particular difficulty, Mr. Ostreni, please indicate that fact. And I will, as indicated, try to read as carefully as I can. But let me ask you this general question first. Is it the case, Mr. Ostreni, that you had not received any of this information as applies to the area of Tetovo, of Brezno, and of Aracinovo because you were in fact just a place man within the so-called Main Staff of the NLA without any real function. Is that what the situation was at the time?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who didn't have any certain factions at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm putting a proposition to you, Mr. Ostreni, which you can accept or not. But my proposition is, the reason why you did not receive any of that information, about what your colleagues were involved in is because in fact you were kept totally out of the actual functioning of your organisation and merely served to provide a face of military legitimacy to an otherwise criminal organisation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, do I have the right to know who kept me isolated as the Defence counsel is putting it to me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you can deal with adequately, Mr. Ostreni, if it is your view, by saying that you weren't kept isolated in your understanding. That isn't correct. It's being put to you as an idea, and if you don't agree with the idea, you can say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Then I'm not. I do not agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Mr. Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please turn to the next page of this document. And if the registry could scroll down a little bit to a paragraph which starts in the middle of the page with the word: "The mission is most likely." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, I will read another passage from that document to you and then ask you a question about it. The says the following: "As of 23 July, the mission has received credible allegations that 25 persons have disappeared or are allegedly detained by the ethnic Albanian armed group operating in the Tetovo area. This number includes ethnic Macedonian civilians and ethnic Albanians who are serving in the Ministry of Interior as regular officers or as reservists at the time of their disappearance. It does not include three persons held by the ethnic Albanian armed group in Kaduca [sic]." My question is this, Mr. Ostreni: Did you have or did you receive any information from the people in your organisation about 25 persons having been detained or kidnapped in the area of Tetovo, in the course of the month of July of 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive any information of that kind during the war; only after the signing of the Ohrid Agreement when it was made public through the media that these persons were being sought. But I did not have any information who carried out this act, who was kidnapped. So in one word, I did not have any such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D1025, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is another document that comes from the organisation known as the OSCE. It's entitled spot report. It's dated the 25th of July of 2001, Skopje. And it covers the period between 10.00 a.m. on the 25th of July and 1800 o'clock on the same day. And I will ask the registry, please, to scroll down to the bottom of the document. Thank you. Mr. Ostreni, there's a section in this document that is entitled comment, and the OSCE in that section records the following. I will read it out to you and then ask you a couple of questions. It says this: "Ethnic Albanian armed group, threatening people in both Jegunovce and Vratnica, to the north of Tetovo has been reported and is being taken seriously. In each case, villagers have been reportedly told to leave or risk being shot, and in Vratnica the threat was apparently directed against police remaining in the village to provide protection for the population." And my question to you, Mr. Ostreni, is the same.
