Did you receive any information from the people in your organisation that this sort of activity was going on in the north of Tetovo in July of 2001 and, in particular, in the two villages that I've mentioned?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't receive information.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you would agree, I hope, that if these actions in fact took place, they would, again, be quite contrary to humanitarian law and the orders which you say Mr. Ahmeti gave to comply with these standards. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that such activities did or did not take place in the locations you mentioned. All I'm saying is that I didn't have any such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. Ostreni. And I'm not trying to suggest that you had that information. But would you agree that if these incidents indeed occurred as they are recorded here, this would, again, indicate a violations of the humanitarian standards which you have mentioned earlier and a violation also of the order you say Mr. Ostreni -- Mr. Ahmeti, I apologise, gave to the members of your organisation to respect those standards. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the initial part, when you said that whether I agreed or not, I do not agree with that. And I again want to point out that I have no information about such activities that you are putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So just to clarify, Mr. Ostreni, and please correct me if I'm misunderstanding what you are saying, are you suggesting that the activities which are recorded in this document do not constitute a violations of humanitarian law and of the order of Mr. Ahmeti, or are you saying something different? And, again, if this incident occurred.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I would like to point out the fact that you only put to me a fragment of this document. Secondly, if someone acted against the human rights and freedom, of course that is not in conformity with the rules of service of the National Liberation Army and of course, those people should have held responsible, but I didn't have any such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that as of July of 2001 another area which you say was under the -- your control is the area around the village of Matejce. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that was an area that was under the so-called control of the 114th Brigade led by Mr. Bushi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of 1st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. And Mr. Bushi, Mr. Ostreni, was at the time the so-called commander of the 114th Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he would one of the persons with whom you would have daily phone conversations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And during those regular phone conversation, did Mr. Bushi tell that you members of his organisation were ethnically cleansing the area in which he was active. Did he ever tell you that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D1103, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is, again, a document known as an investigator's notes. It's a document prepared by the Office of the Prosecutor as a result of an interview which the Prosecutor conducted on the 7th of July of 2001 in Macedonia. And I'll read a number of passages to you. The documents records the following: "On the 25th of July, 2001, early in the morning, I was in my house in Matejce together with six other people. About 10 UCK soldiers in camouflage uniforms came to the house and ordered us to leave the house." Then I will go a bit further in the second paragraph. It says this: "One of the UCK men introduced himself, the commander. He said he was coming from Kosovo. He took me to a separate room and started to ask questions about my children, saying that I was lying. He hit me twice in my face and threatened to kill me with his knife. He then took me back to the others. "Later many UCK soldiers, I would say at least 50, came to see us at the mosque, where they had their lunch. They used to curse us and at some stage everybody who was passing came to hit us. We also had to beat each other and if we didn't hit hard enough, the UCK soldiers were beating us. "One of the soldiers tried to hit my head with the barrel of his Kalashnikov, but I managed to protect my head with my hand and he hit my wrist. I still have serious problems with the wrist. I was also kicked on my stomach and my leg. At some stage, they moved to us a dark room where the soldier also used to come to beat us." And then in the last paragraph this person says this, that: "I don't know the perpetrators. I think that some of the young UCK members were from Matejce but I don't know their names." Mr. Ostreni, during your telephone conversations with Mr. Bushi did he ever tell you that that sort of things was happening in the area in which his so-called brigade was being active?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct also, Mr. Ostreni, that another location in which you -- your organisation was active is the area around the monastery of Lesok. Are you in agreement with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is included in the map that I gave to NATO.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the leader or commander of the local brigade there was a man by the name of Daut Rexhepi, is that correct, known as Komandant Leka. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not a brigade commander. He was a battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is he one of the person with whom you would have contacts as part of your function as a Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I maintained contacts with the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you say who was the commander of that brigade at the time, during the crisis period?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean of 112th Brigade, right, it was Commander Iliri or Isa Lika.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And during your conversations you said you had with that person, did he tell you also that the same sort of activities as we have just seen, mistreatment of civilians, expulsions of civilian, intimidation and so on, did he inform you that he was also -- the members of his brigade were also carrying out that sort of activities in his area?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D1028, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is, again, a -- the record of an interview taken by the Office of the Prosecutor with a person from Macedonia. It's dated -- in fact, it is undated, but in the text it appears that it was taken in -- I'm sorry, it's May 2003 and the text referred to another meeting in April of 2003, and the person who was interviewed said the following to the Office of the Prosecutor. "On 3 April 2003 Darko Boskoski statement had been taken in Skopje ICTY field office. It followed from the above statement that the person called Boro had been another victim kidnapped by NLA and kept in the same prison as Boskoski." And then in the next paragraph it records the following: "On 7 July 2001 at 3.30 p.m. heavy shooting had been taking place in the area of Tetovo. The witness got a phone call from his brother giving him advice to leave the house and meet each other nearby Lesok fuel station. As the witness drove his car in the distance about to 150 metre from his house in Dzepciste, he was stopped by four men in green camouflage colour trousers and black shirts with NLA patch on the sleeves. Three of them were armed with Kalashnikov and one with RPG." And if we can turn to the next page, please. And the person -- please, at the -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The person continues by saying this to the Office of the Prosecutor: "Lada Niva car without licence plate arrived to the scene 15 minutes later. The driver of the above car brought Daut Rexhepi aka Komandant Leka. The witness identified him later in TV, later on in TV. Leka addressed the witness, saying, Do you know me? Where are you going? Leka wore camouflage green uniform. The witness had been taken into the house of certain Nevzat, red in colour, built in brick. In the room under the staircase Leka started beating the witness with fists and kicking him with legs. Then they tied up the witness's hands behind the back using plastic handcuffs and they put bag on his head." And then he continues describing the scene of beating to which he was subjected.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry to turn to page 1D00-8416. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The person says this: "Then from the house they took him to neighbouring stable where they -- where he remained overnight. The stable built the stones and no livestock inside. Then he was taken to the basement of the NLA HQ, where he was again interviewed and brutally beaten by the photograph whilst the second NLA soldier had been guarding. Then he was taken back to the stable with handcuffed hands behind the back and with the bag on his head. They forced him to walk in the circles to lose orientation. During day-time they came about five people. They tore the victim's blue shirt and beat him with cable on the naked body." And it says that "Darko Boskoski later found the shirt, as he had been kept in the same stable." "Then one the offenders threatened him with gun and with knife. The victim was also badly beaten that he could not see through swollen eyes and sometimes fainted." Mr. Ostreni, is it -- did you receive any information about mistreatment carried out by members of your organisation in the area around Lesok during your conversation with so-called commander of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of any measures that were taken by the so-called commander to punish the people who had been involved in this incident?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, that question blatantly assumes the correctness. We've been sitting, listening for some time to interviews in which people suggest things have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will rephrase it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let it be clear that's not proof that those things have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You put it to the witness simply to get the answer that he knew nothing of it at the time. The impression is created that these things are fact. Now, let it be clear so you --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, my question --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- won't be misled and these listening are not misled that these are not established facts. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, assuming that this events occur and, as indicated by Judge Parker, this is simply the statement of a witness taken by the Office of the Prosecutor, but assuming that this incident occur, would you agree that this would be contrary, again, to the standard of humanitarian law that you said your organisation complied with. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it would be contrary, and I'm really surprised why measures were not taken against those who carried out these acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that in fact your organisation, earlier on in its existence, had made it quite clear what its real purpose was and its real purpose was to create areas that would be under the sole control of the NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you're doing injustice to me by posing this question. The brigades were formed from smaller group, squads, platoons, companies. Later on battalions were formed and the brigade gets its shape. And by expanding it gradually establishes its authority in the area where it's operating. As a territory or area of responsibility of a brigade, I'm saying is that they had this task to perform, to go out to their positions, starting from the squads up to the brigade level, because, for example, if there are ten persons, they can spread to 150 metres. If we're talking about a brigade with three battalions, then it would cover a territory of 17 kilometres. So this is an area under battalion, under a brigade, and if you're asking me about these things, I've provided you with maps which contain the positions and the tasks that were issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps my question was not so clear, Mr. Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how I understood your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will try to rephrase it in a different way. Is it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that your claim in this courtroom and in your statement that the NLA's purpose and goal was to promote the human rights of the ethnic Albanians in Macedonia was just a facade whereas in fact your goal and as originally stated by your organisation was to keep and acquire areas that would be under the control of your organisation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That cannot be correct, because you missed the goal of taking a certain area under control. The goal of the NLA is clearly and explicitly explained in communique number 6 that we discussed early and in the memorandum, as well as in all other communiques that we issued. The demands of the NLA were addressed in a way so that pressure is made on the state and the state organs sit and discuss and guarantee the rights and freedoms of the Albanians in the Republic of Macedonia, as well as members of other ethnic communities. These are the goals of the NLA, while everything else that you are saying and putting to me as alleged goals of the NLA, that is your opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, could you perhaps explain how the ethnic cleansing of non-ethnic Albanians from particular areas would promote the rights and freedom of the Albanians in the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe your question is a little bit provocative. The National Liberation Army calls all the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia as such, citizens of the Republic of Macedonia, and its goal then and now was co-existence. The problem of the Macedonian population moving from their area, even in the view of the representative of the Macedonian army expressed in his book was that in that time, a propaganda was launched which got a contrary effect, saying that in fact the army was not able to protect the Macedonian population where it lived. Then, the distribution of weapons by the police to the civilians, with a purpose of them, the civilians, defending themselves, you can find proof to what you're -- of what I'm saying in the book of the late General that was leading the Macedonian army. In this book, he describes how he was summoned by the president of the state to hear from the citizens of Tetovo how the police distributed them with weapons and ammunition and how the police told them that these weapons and ammunition was for their self-defence. All this happened before the 25th of July. Please, I might not be very precise on the date because I don't remember all of them. For these reasons, on the 25th and 26th July, in the evening the NLA went and collected weapons that were distributed to the civilians in these villages by the police. This is all written in the book written by the late General. Further, the academy of science, with its silent position that Macedonia should be partitioned and raising the issue of changing the population, this all caused distrust and insecurity among the population and gave way to displacement of the population. So there were a series of activities that resulted in insecurity, because it sent a signal that those citizens would not be safe, and that's why they, the citizens, left. This is very well described in the book that I just mentioned. These are the reasons, in addition to the fact that a war was going on and combat was going on in areas where all citizens of Macedonia lived, not only Macedonians and Albanians. So these were signals saying that the army was not ready and able to defend its population and that's why the police distributed weapons. I apologise, Your Honours, for not being brief on this issue, but I just felt that I needed to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ostreni. And I think you've referred to what you said were the stated goals of the NLA in a communique known as communique number 6. Do you that agree that prior to communique number 6 there had been at least two previous communiques. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already stated, I arrived from the United States on the 26th of February. I was on the plane on that date. I went to the KPC in Kosova where I worked and I wasn't following closely and fully what was going on prior to 1st of March, before I joined and before I met with Mr. Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But surely, Mr. Ostreni, as a so-called Chief of Staff of the so-called NLA, you would have known about communique number 4. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will help jog your memory a bit. Do you recall that towards the end of January of 2001 a group of men who called themselves the NLA at the time, attacked a police station in the village which we've been talking about earlier, the village of Tearce? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated earlier, during this time I was staying with my daughter in the United States. I left all my work aside, especially this side. I was not involved in this at that time. I was Chief of Staff of the KPC. I went to the States for a visit to have a rest. All my family is there. I have relatives on my side and on my wife's side. So basically I didn't show interest in these matters, because I went to the states just to have a rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But surely when you arrived in March of 2001, Mr. Ahmeti or someone else in that organisation would have shown you communique number 4, which took responsibility for the attack in Tearce. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't told this, and I didn't ask either.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And surely someone in your organisation would have told that you in this particular communique of the end of January of 2001, your organisation referred to the Macedonians as the occupiers. Did anyone tell you that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're claiming that this is what happened, that he told me that, and I'm claiming on my part that did he not tell me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't the truth, Mr. Ostreni, that your communiques were just the flavour of the month that you adapted with a view to increase or in fact to acquire some support from the international community by always changing your goals and stated purposes? Isn't that the truth?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is not clear to me. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. Isn't it correct that the real purpose of your organisation was stated in that communique, communique number 4, and that what came afterwards, including communique number 6, which we've -- you've referred to, is just a public relation exercise by Mr. Ahmeti, in particular, to make your organisation look like a legitimate army, quote/unquote. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that. I abide by communique number 6 and the following communiques, because at that time I was close, I was in Kosovo, and I started to work with Mr. Ali Ahmeti. Whatever happened before communique number 6, I'm not familiar with that part, because I was not in Europe.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the record the communique number 4 may be found in the so-called "White Book" of the Ministry of Interior. It is exhibit P45.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, do you recall that yesterday you suggested in this courtroom that one of the purpose of the NLA or one of its goals was to see a democracy arise in Macedonia similar to that, and I think you mentioned Switzerland and Belgium. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but you're using my statement in a different context. What I said is the following. We need -- needed international intervention, international assistance in carrying out negotiations with the Macedonian government. This is stated in the memorandum and I've made the statement when we discussed the memorandum. However, as we were not in a position to reach agreement between the sides, we need the assistance and the intervention of the international community. The development of the situation proves that we received this intervention and this assistance and through this assistance we managed to sign the Ohrid Agreement, the mobilisation and put an end to the war, and to create the conditions for living as a free and equal citizens in the Republic of Macedonia. This is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for the clarification, Mr. Ostreni, but I will stay for a second with the example of Belgium which you gave yesterday, and you may be aware from the news these days that some political problems in Belgium and lingering tensions between its communities. Have you been following that in the newspaper?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I think you have something else on your mind. The example of Belgium and Switzerland was mentioned by us in order to show that in Macedonia, just like Belgium and Switzerland and other western European countries an agreement can be reached, co-existence can function in conditions of equality between the citizens, in conditions when Macedonia would be the wealth and property, not only of the ethnic Macedonians but of all its citizens, when Macedonia would be a multi-ethnic state and not a single ethnic state. In this context, I mentioned Holland and example of Switzerland but only as an explanation to the memorandum.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that, but would you agree with that, Mr. Ostreni, that if tomorrow a group of disgruntled and violent French-speaking Belgian were to blow up police station and kill police officers, they would be arrested as criminals. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why you're asking me about this state. You can ask me questions about my state. I'm witness for that purpose here and by profession I'm not an attorney. To satisfy your question, I'm only here to speak about things that I know, I saw, or heard. It is not up to me to reach conclusions what would happen in each and every individual case. I'm not competent for those issues. So I would kindly ask you to refer to me as a witness, not as an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if -- I will try to formulate it in such a way that I'm not asking you a legal judgment, Mr. Ostreni. That's fair enough of you. But would you agree that it would only be logical that if, tomorrow, someone in Belgium shot and murdered a police officer, he or she would be arrested as a criminal. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what you're asking me about. You're asking me about Belgium, if someone kills someone else. There's a judicial system in place there, and measures are taken pursuant to that judicial system. And I really am not competent to speak on behalf of the honourable state as Belgium as to what would happen to someone in the case that you described, I'm not here to testify about Belgium.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But perhaps can you agree with that. That if the person who shot that policeman had sat for a few hours at his or her computer and typed up a number of rules and regulation, he or she would also be likely to end up before the -- what you call the judicial system of Belgium. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're saying so. Personally I'm not an attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, may I ask to you wait a moment. The Chamber has to intervene, Mr. Mettraux, to suggest that it cannot for the world see how it is going to be helped by such a grossly general and incomplete example as you are giving based on a theoretical situation in another country. We've got to look at the facts as they existed in Macedonia at the relevant time, all the facts and then deal with some very difficult factual and legal questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will move on back to the Macedonian, since the witness has indicated that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I did interrupt Ms. Regue or not give her a chance to speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I was going to say something similar such as the terms you were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, let's go back to Macedonia then. And you indicated, I believe, that you had given specific instructions or -- instructions I think was your term to the members of your organisation to respect religious buildings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that citizens along with their properties should be respected. Speaking of religious sites, we shouldn't even discuss it all because we Albanians pray to God in three ways, as Catholics, as Orthodox, and as Muslims. We marry with other religious communities like with Orthodox and Christians and there is harmony, religious harmony prevails among Albanians in general. Not a single Albanian would have raised his or her hand. If he did, he would lose the respect of his family, his circle of relatives and friends so if he did that against some religious site. Even now in Macedonia, in Tetovo and other countries -- other places, Albanians help Macedonians, even donating money to repair the churches. I would kindly ask you to understand our idea of preserving religious facilities. Anyone who was caused damage to such a facility, that would run counter to the morale of his family and Albanians in general. And that would be contrary to the rules of NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Did you ever become aware or did you ever receive information from the members of your organisation that these orders of Mr. Ostreni [sic] were -- Ahmeti and -- or the instructions that you gave were being ignored and that in fact religious facilities were being disrespected by members of your organisation. Did you ever receive that information?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not receive such an information. I did receive information that mosques were torched. Albanian families were damaged in -- like in Manastir, in Prilep, that a large number of mosques were burned like the one in Prilep. I received such information, but I regret to say that the information was to the effect that Albanian religious sites were being constantly damaged. We can prove this whenever you want. You can visit them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, in answer to my question, you received no information that members of your organisation had been involved in causing damage to any such religious properties. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't, until the end of 2001, after the agreement and so on. I did not receive any information about the damages. The only information I received after the war through the media and the television was that I have seen, and I'm sorry to say this, that in Matejce there were some markings -- graffiti saying NLA, but that can be -- that could have been done by anyone. This is the information I have but I didn't receive it true the chain of command during the time the NLA brigade was active. Only -- it was only after it was [indiscernible] liberated, the journalists entered it, it was then that I learned that the word NLA was written on a fresco but I learned it from the journalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D828, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is another one of these reports prepared by the OSCE. This one is dated the 29th of August of 2001, and it comes from the archives of the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like to ask the registry to go to page 1D00-7226, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, I will read to you what the report notes under paragraph 3, please. Thank you. It says this: "The effect of the destruction by internal explosion of the Lesok monastery to the north of Tetovo was widely condemned, including by the OSCE. A feared violent backlash did not occur, although public anger and frustration was evident. The ethnic Albanian armed group issued a press release condemning the attack and disavowing involvement." Mr. Ostreni, did you receive any information from anyone in your organisation that someone from the NLA had been involved in that destruction?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not, in answer to your question, but at the time that this very bad incident occurred, about which we expressed our indignation then and now, was the time when after the 26th of August, we had a great problem regarding the collection and voluntarily surrender of weapons. I was asked at that time by the journalist who asked me the same question that you did and my reply to them was: If we had to damage such a facility like the Lesok one, we would have done that at the time when the fighting was going on and not at the time when we are trying to hand in the first contingent of weapons and continue with the others and move on to peace. So this is a very bad thing, something which shouldn't have been done, but I think that it was - and it is - a duty of the competent bodies to investigate into that and find out who the perpetrator was. We would all be very happy for the perpetrator to be brought to justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you ever become aware that members of your organisation, the NLA, used religious buildings, including mosques as facilities for military purposes?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not directly there during the wartime to come to such a conclusion. But the brigade was in well-known positions, the positions which were open to anyone until late. Everybody could see where they were. The members of the NLA wanted to be far, to be positioned far in places where they couldn't be hit by the shelling, by the military and the police. So they couldn't stay, couldn't be positioned in such facilities that you are putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let me read what the report of the OSCE goes on to say. It's at the bottom of the same page. It says this: "Monitors noted that in Tetovo the ethnic Albanian armed group placed a firing position in the immediate vicinity of the historic painted mosque and dug trenches and opened" - if can you turn to the next page - "And opened firing portals in the wall of the historic Muslim Teke. Exchanges of fire in both of these locations could have severely damaged the sites." Mr. Ostreni, did you ever receive information from members of your organisation that they had in fact placed a firing position in the immediate vicinity of the painted mosque near Tetovo and opened firing portals in the walls of the historic Muslim Teke? Is that information that was given to you during the crisis?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you be more explicit? Do you mean one or two such facilities?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I can ask you this. Were you aware of either of the incidents which I've read out to you, either the Muslim Teke or the incident related to the painted mosque?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So you are implying that we are talking of a mosque and the Teke. These are two different buildings or facilities. I knew that the unit of Tetovo Brigade with the consent of the father who worked in the Teke placed a firing position, because nearby at the graveyard was a police check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree, I hope, that this would again be contrary to humanitarian law and also to the instructions which you say were sent down the chain of command. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't make an assessment of that. I'm not a lawyer. The important thing is that that position operated there for a period of time and it was placed with the approval or the consent of the father who was responsible for the Teke.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I think we may need to have the break, Mr. Mettraux. We will resume at quarter past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, when we left off, I was asking you about military facilities placed in the vicinity or inside religious building and I would like to follow up on that. Would you agree that there was no good military reason for the NLA to place those military facilities close to religious buildings but that in fact the reason for you to do so was to use any reaction by the Macedonian forces for propaganda purposes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. And I don't know whether there was any such military position in the painted mosque, because it was a matter of a squad. It was a very low hierarchy for me to know. But I know that the leader of the Teke who is called Father, in agreement with the NLA unit, allowed them to enter the yard, and as I heard, it's simply that I heard it, they entered the yard in order to protect it from the police force and the army forces because they feared that they might destroy this particular one, as they had destroyed other religious buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D19, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is, again, a document prepared by the OSCE and it was given to us by the Office of the Prosecutor. And the title of this document is: Human rights developments and it covers the period 1st August 2001 to the 15th of August of 2001. I'm going ask of you a few questions of this document, Mr. Ostreni, but I'd like at this stage to turn to the third page of that document. That would be 1D00-1606. Thank you. And, Mr. Ostreni, I'm going to read to you a paragraph from the report of the OSCE that started with the words: "Two further observations." I will read that to you and then I will ask you a question. "Two further observations are also important. There has been a clear tendency on the part of the Tetovo NLA to use religious and historic sites as military installations or bases of operations. Military emplacements are also located in positions where they are of fire includes religious and historic sites. There is particular concern for the painted mosque and the Teke monastery. The misuse of religious sites as military installations must be condemned. It should be noted that in the case of the Teke, it appears the NLA was attempting to force the Macedonian forces to fire on the site for propaganda purposes." Mr. Ostreni, do you agree that contrary to what you suggested of the authorisation of the local father, what the member of your organisation were doing with the Teke is to shoot from the monastery, in the hope that the Macedonian authorities would fire back with a view for you to then use that for propaganda purposes. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with that. Because it was not only the Teke that was attacked by the army and the police forces but all the -- all the mosques in the area where Brigade 113 was located and they have caused -- inflicted great damage on them. I think that the Father of the Teke aimed at preventing the forces from coming near it. We sat down with him at a cafe, Ali Ahmeti was there and some other friends, and he said that he was very happy that his Teke was not damaged but we, too, were very happy. This was a portal at a very further wall -- farthest wall of the Teke which was across the police point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So your evidence, Mr. Ostreni, is that the statement made by the OSCE about what they understood to be happening in or around the Teke was incorrect?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand that. Can you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. The statement that I've read from the report of the OSCE, you disagree with the conclusions that I've read from you for that -- for you from that report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree only with the concern raised by this institution but not with the particular part that you are putting to me, because I don't understand this document. I haven't read this document myself. So what you put to me, namely that the NLA entered there to provoke fire from the Macedonian forces, with this part, I do not agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And you've also indicated earlier today that one of the prohibitions that was made clear in your instructions to members of your organisation was the prohibition on sexual violence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. That applies to all honest citizens. Nobody would do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you ever receive reports from members of your organisation that actually members of the NLA had been involved in such crimes?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. But if you allow me, Your Honour, to explain something in this regard, the NLA and in real terms Brigade 112 took measures to close down all the facilities where there were such, where women worked there. So the NLA did the opposite of what are you putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please turn to the previous page of this document. That would be 1D00-1605.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Ostreni, I will read to you a passage that starts from a rather large paragraph in the middle of that page with the word "the most disturbing indication." I will read it out to you. It says this: "The most disturbing indication of a decline in NLA discipline and professionalism is the incident on August 7 in which five ethnic Macedonian construction workers were kidnapped whilst working on the new highway between Skopje and Tetovo. Although the mission successfully encouraged local villagers to let these innocent civilians go, later that night, their treatment during the 15 hours they were held by the NLA was shocking. According to interviews with men and the mission's observations of their condition upon their release, 25 to 30 uniformed members of the NLA not only severely beat them with shovels but also mutilated several of the men's backs with knife, forced a number of to commit oral sodomy on each other and sexually abused at least two of the men with objects. According to the released men the NLA unit that seized and abused them was comprised of ethnic Albanians from Tetovo and a local village and under a local commander." Mr. Ostreni, this incident which is often referred to as the Mavrovo rural workers case, is it something which members of your organisation brought to your attention at the time when it happened?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the registry please turn to the next page, again. I'd like to read another passage from the same document, Mr. Ostreni. This is the last -- I'm sorry, the last-but-one paragraph which starts with the word "finally it should be noted," and I will read it out to you. "Finally it should be noted that investigation of human rights related incidents is complicated by the problem that the NLA is applying pressure to its own people and must be considered as a possible source of human rights abuses to ethnic Albanians, including beatings and murders." Mr. Ostreni, was any such case of members of your organisation applying pressure on to ethnic Albanians, including beatings and murders, ever brought to your attention by members of your organisation?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that as a high-ranking members of the so-called NLA, you also followed the statements and view which were expressed by the international community about your organisation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until we surrendered weapons, I had contacts when I did have such contacts with NATO. And I could not follow up every developments. I was very, very busy. The document you are putting to me, I don't even see the date. If you want to help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The date, sir, that appears on the top of the document is the 17th August of 2001, which is apparently the date at which it was faxed but the document covers the period between the 1st and the 15th of August of 2001. But staying for a second on the issue, you've indicated that you had contacts with NATO, so I will focus on NATO.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this time that you are putting to me, I was working to prepare the plans on the surrender of weapons, to define the locations where such weapons should be collected. I took care that soldiers didn't leave without handing in the weapons, because it was a time when the Ohrid Framework Agreement was signed, and I was afraid that the soldiers might misunderstand it that the war was over, why should I remain here, not go home, why should I remain in difficult conditions when I could go home. So these were concerns that I had to deal with at that time. There were about 5.000 soldiers involved of whom, as I said, we had to collect 3.383 weapons. 3.856 -- 57 we collected, and to do that, we had to do a lot of work. And this is where I concentrated most of my efforts without neglecting the efforts made by other organisations, be them NGOs or other government organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that, but, Mr. Ostreni, did you become aware during your earlier meeting, you say with NATO at a time when you were not busy surrendering weapons that they had asked to you stop intimidating civilians and ask you to leave the village which you occupied. Do you recall any such statement being made by NATO?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are using terms which NATO didn't use. You are saying villages that were occupied by the NLA. You cannot occupy your own country, sir, but the NLA had established its authority over these villages in the agreement signed between the Chief of Staff of the NLA and representatives of NATO. We agreed on the proposal made by Peter Feith and Ali Ahmeti that our units not remain inside the villages. And in fact, they were in between, in areas in between the villages, and we took all the measures to remain where it was allowed to be, based on the agreement approved by Peter Feith and Ali Ahmeti, and then of course they agreed -- had another agreement reached with the representatives of the army and the police, which was signed on the 5th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we will come back, Mr. Ostreni, on the Prizren agreement, as it is known, as well as the cease-fire agreement on the 5th of July. But for the time I would like to show you Rule 65 ter 1D891, please. Mr. Ostreni, this is a document, an official document that comes from NATO. It is a statement by the Secretary-General of NATO at the time was Mr. George Robertson concerning developments in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia and it is dated the 11th of June of 2001. And I'd like to read to you the first paragraph of that document. It says this: "I strongly condemn the latest actions by extremist groups in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia and denounce their threats of further attacks. The escalation of violence cannot bring a positive outcome. I urge extremists to end their fighting, leave the villages they are occupying, and cease the intimidation of innocent civilians. Violence does not serve justice, nor does it contribute to the establishment of a better and fair society." Mr. Ostreni, were you aware of this call being made by the Secretary-General of NATO on the 11th of June of 2001 for you to stop the intimidation of civilians and for to you leave the village which you were occupying. Can you recall that statement?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know whether it's written here, of the civilians. Can you explain to me where is this word "the civilians"? Maybe it will be easier for me to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will read it again to you, Mr. Ostreni, which is the third sentence of that first paragraph, and I will read it more slowly perhaps. It says this: "I urge extremists to end their fighting, leave the villages they are occupying, and cease the intimidation of innocent civilians." Now do you recall the Secretary-General of NATO making that call on -- on you, on the 11th of June of 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he made several statements and that he was committed to the solution of this issue, so I have to take your word for that, because, as I said, I cannot read it in my own language. So I presume it is what you are putting to me and I'm sure that Mr. Solana was held in high esteem by us. He sought solutions to the crisis and when later on he held news conferences he spoke about putting an end to the conflict but he doesn't refer to us anymore as criminals. Maybe there is another document that shows what I'm saying, where he says that: We call them armed groups, which, in resolution 90/20 of the European commission, the NLA was no longer called armed groups, but armed formations, and I believe this is what he called us. In our statements, public statements, we have always declared that we accept the instructions and advice of the international community, but on the condition that our freedoms and rights are fulfilled in the Republic of Macedonia. This is the way we went, until we reached the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement on the 13th of August, so I believe what you are saying to me, that Solana has said what you put to me he has.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I believe it would be Mr. Robertson who said that as Secretary-General of NATO. But do you agree, Mr. Ostreni, that a month and a half later the same organisation, NATO, was still calling upon you to stop the intimidation and kidnapping of civilians. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that. It is impossible for me to recall every single detail, but of course you're most welcome to refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D897, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is, again, a -- this time a press statement by the Secretary-General of NATO, still at the time Mr. Robertson, and this one is dated the 24th of July of 2001. And in the first paragraph it says: "Maintaining the cease-fire in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia is of prime importance. I urge both parties to stick to their commitments of 5 July. Provocations and encroachments are unacceptable and must stop. In particular, I call on the so-called NLA to revert to their position at the time of their cease-fire undertakings. They must show respect for the safety of the civil population. Intimidation and kidnapping must end and the Jezince-Tetovo road must be free from roadblock." Mr. Ostreni, does that help refresh your memory as of 24th of July of 2001 that Mr. Robertson was still calling on you to stop the intimidation and kidnapping of members of the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The NATO General-Secretary of course assisted us with his recommendations and instructions as I see it here and to my recollection, I will again refer to the book of Pande Petrovski. It is 24th of July, 18 days after the proclamation of cease-fire. During this period of time, weapons were distributed to Macedonian citizens along the Tetovo-Jezince road and that's why the NLA entered on the 25th and on the 25th and 26th Ali Ahmeti give an order and insisted that members who had entered in those villages should return. There is information in the book of Pande Petrovski, a person who led the war at that time, that this is a period during which such provocations were made with the distribution of weapons, and that's why it was necessary for Mr. Robertson to made these recommendation in order to follow the agreement between us and the forces of the ARM and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, I'm grateful for your answer. You've already given that indication on a number of occasion earlier. But my question was more limited in scope, and the question was whether, on the 24th or on or around the 24th of July of 2001 in any case, you were aware of calls made by the Secretary-General of NATO to the effect that your organisation should stop the intimidation and kidnapping of members of the civilian population. Were you aware of that call?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of this call, yes. But this does not show who kidnapped whom. We were not in a position to undertake any measures against a person just on basis of this communique. In general, things like this can happen in a war, like our war, between the NLA and the armed forces of the Republic of Macedonia, and that's why the NATO Secretary-General made these recommendations and instructions so that both sides were aware of these issues and become more careful in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I do take your answer to suggest that no one member of the NLA was punished for intimidating or kidnapping members of the civilian population in the year of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I wanted to say, because I don't want to express myself in advance, I'm waiting for your questions first. But as the situation developed there were certain provocations instigated by the then government of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, Mr. Ostreni. But the question was slightly different and I will try to reformulate it. In your previous answer you said that this -- commenting on the document you said: This does not show who kidnapped whom, we were not in a position to undertake any measures against a person just on the basis of his communique. My question, follow-up question was, whether, to your knowledge, any member of your organisation, the National Liberation Army, was ever arrested and punished for acts of intimidation and kidnapping of members of the civilian population to the extent that this is within your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I think that the witness said that he didn't know who kidnapped whom, basically, so first I think that the knowledge should be established whether he is aware of these facts and secondly, if he is aware of the facts, whether disciplinary measures were taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I understood the witness to have said that he had knowledge of the call having been made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have a very different understanding of his evidence from you, Mr. Mettraux. I understood him to be saying that this started by distribution of arms by the Macedonian government forces, which then led to certain incidents which then led to Ali Ahmeti calling on the people to withdraw -- his people to withdraw from those incidents. So perhaps you'd better explore just what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, did you have any knowledge of members of your organisation having been involved in cases of intimidation and kidnapping of members of the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that during the conflict, when you were caught red-handed - and I mean you not personally but your organisation or members of the organisation you were a member of - were caught committing a crime, you tried to justify it on the basis that it was justified from a military point of view. Do you recall any such incidents?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You were talking in general terms. You're not naming a crime. It is only a pronoun that doesn't show much in itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I'll ask you this, then. Do you know what happened in the town or the village of Vejce on the 28th of April of 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Vejce, but at the location called Tepisate, which is between Vejce and Selce villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I am grateful for the specification, Mr. Ostreni. And is it correct that what happened on this location is that a vehicle of the army was ambushed by members of your organisations and that after the ambush, the survivors were executed or that the bodies of the dead were shot at or given further stab wounds. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it wasn't just one vehicle there. There were two Hermelins there, and two Lada Nivas, to what I can tell, the Defence counsel is not well familiar with the situation, and I'm trying to help him. It is true that they were ambushed by a NLA unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm very grateful for the specification, Mr. Ostreni. Are you also aware of the fact that after one of the vehicle had been blown up in the ambush, the survivors were then executed and apparently one of them burnt alive and the others shot at or knifed by members of the NLA. Is that something that you're familiar with?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have knowledge, but not in the way you're putting it to me. I know that they fell in an ambush, they were soldiers, they had their leaders, they were armed, and they fell in an ambush. Weapons that caused the vehicles to catch fire were used. If a person is in a vehicle when it catches fire, of course that -- that person will be burned as well. This ambush involved a close range -- close-distance fighting and weapons that they had with them were used. In order to discuss this event, which I feel sorry to explain here, because we have to create goodwill and trust, but we are here to shed light on these events. Events should be followed as early as the 14th of March to see how the situation developed and then under the light of the operation MX of the Macedonian forces against the NLA. That is against the 112th Brigade and this is how we should look at the killing of the 16-year-old child in Selce and then discuss this ambush.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that. At this stage we'll stay with the incident in Vejce and I will ask you a question, a simple question whether you know or not, that Ali Ahmeti, shortly after the incident in Vejce took responsibility for the attack and justified it on the basis that the NLA had acted in self-defence. Are you aware of Mr. Ahmeti saying that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what Mr. Ali Ahmeti said at that time, but I remember the event, how it happened. I remember that the units, every now and then, during that time, the units of the ARM, in combination with police force, painted -- would go out in those village, intimidate the villagers and the culmination was reached when the 16-year-old young man was killed and this event gave rise to the act undertaken by the NLA unit against the patrol which, to my recollection, consists of 13 or 14 members.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is exhibit P45 at page N005-7606-0225, and in the Macedonian version it would be at NO01-5238 , please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, the document which I'm about to show to you is a so-called "White Book" prepared by the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Macedonia. Hopefully the document will be shown to you as well in Macedonian. There is no Albanian translation, but I will read to you the document. This would be, I believe, the next page in the Macedonian version, please. Oh, I'm sorry, it's the right page but on the right side in the Macedonian. I apologise, the previous page on the right side of the page. Yes, thank you. On the right side, please. And on the top. Thank you. Mr. Ostreni, that may help refresh your memory. There's a report contained in this document which is entitled: "Ali Ahmeti: We killed in Self-defence," and it says this: "Ethnic Albanian rebels said today that they had acted in self-defence in a clash in which eight Macedonian security troops were killed on Saturday. "The political leader of the rebel National Liberation Army, UCK, Ali Ahmeti, told Reuter by telephone 'We consider it as a provocation by the Macedonian forces so that they could present themself as victims -- as victim.' "Ahmeti says the UCK rebels opened fire in self-defence after Macedonian troops approached their positions. He says no UCK soldiers were killed or wounded during the clash." And the report is dated 30 April 2001 and comes from Tirana. Can you recall, Mr. Ostreni, Mr. Ahmeti making any such statement in relation to the incident in Vejce?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honourable counsel, Ali Ahmeti, first of all, would never say when NLA rebels did this. The word "rebel" is unknown to Mr. Ali Ahmeti, and this gives me doubts about the "White Book", because this book does not mention a single case when the ARM and police forces mistreated civilians and such cases occurred. A person was killed in the middle of Skopje in Lozana pizzeria and this is nowhere mentioned. Then the shops and the houses of the Albanians in Bitola were burnt and there's no mention of it in this book. That's why I think that the time has come for all of us to think differently. It is impossible for Ali Ahmeti to call himself a rebel.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, you are right in this sense, that the inability to give you a copy of that document in your language might have been unfair to you, because the only statement that is indented and is being attributed to Mr. Ahmeti in what I have read is the following, and I will specify that fact: "We consider it as a provocation by the Macedonian forces so that they could present themselves as victim." So you are right, Mr. Ostreni, the reference to rebel is not attributed to Mr. Ahmeti, it seems from that document. But do you agree, or can you remember, Mr. Ahmeti at the time making the suggestion that the attack at Vejce was a response to a provocation by the Macedonian forces. Do you recall him saying that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps do you recall that the international community viewed the attack in Vejce quite differently. And perhaps I should ask you this: Do you recall that the US administration, the state department and the White House described this attack of the NLA in Vejce as senseless act of violence, a barbarous attack, extremist violence and terrorist activity. Do you recall any of those expressions being attached to the attack in Vejce by the US Administration?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, I cannot express this only in terms of if I recall or not a certain events. If I have it somewhere in writing, it would be nice if you show that to me and that would refresh my memory. If the department of United States wrote this, then it is true that they wrote this. I cannot comment on that, whether it is their document or not, without seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that would be a convenient time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would be. We must finish for the week. We resume on Monday morning at 9.00, but we have been moved to Courtroom III. So we adjourn now for the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 12th day of November, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.01 p.m.,
